clips.hook: Leaky gut is an energy problem, not an immune problem
clips.text: Energy deficits in intestinal cells starve them of butyrate, forcing a shift to anaerobic metabolism that releases excess oxygen into the digestive tract.

clips.hook: How Akkermansia and the MUC2 protein maintain the gut lining
clips.text: Specialized bacteria consume sugars within the MUC2 protein layer, producing short-chain fatty acids that stimulate goblet cells to secrete fresh mucus.

clips.hook: The biophysical origin of cellular fatigue
clips.text: Bacterial fragments entering the bloodstream trigger extracellular ATP release, forcing mitochondria into a defensive state that halts normal energy production.

clips.hook: A four-step clinical protocol to rebuild the gut barrier
clips.text: Specific plant compounds like pomegranate extract and cranberry proanthocyanidins are used to nourish beneficial microbes and stimulate protective mucus production.

clips.hook: Why Akkermansia does not destroy your mucus layer
clips.text: A clinical discussion addresses specific exposure timelines and patient data within a structured medical questionnaire.
